title: Compact and Efficient CAM Architecture through Combinatorial Encoding and Self-Terminating Searching for In-Memory-Searching Accelerator
problem: Existing CAM designs use conventional encoding schemes requiring two complementary storage nodes and search signals per bit, with separate precharging and evaluation phases, limiting area and energy efficiency for pattern searching.
motivation: CAM enables highly parallel pattern searching for data-intensive applications, making improvements in area and energy efficiency valuable.
method: The architecture employs a combinatorial encoding scheme that encodes entry/query states using permutations and combinations of multiple storage nodes as a group, rather than individual complementary nodes. It also introduces a self-terminating searching scheme that detects matching conditions during the precharging phase and terminates precharging upon match detection. The design is implemented using ferroelectric FET (FeFET) technology for area-energy-delay co-optimization.
key_novelty: Combinatorial encoding of grouped storage nodes combined with self-terminating search that detects matches during precharging phase rather than in a separate evaluation phase.
contributions: Combinatorial encoding scheme improving encoding efficiency and reducing hardware implementation cost compared to conventional encoding
Self-terminating searching scheme reducing search delay and energy by detecting matches during precharging
FeFET-based implementation achieving 1182X area-energy-delay product improvement over conventional CMOS-based CAM
Co-optimized architecture demonstrating practical in-memory searching accelerator

metrics.ppa: 1182X AEDP reduction vs conventional CMOS-based CAM
